title: vLLM Production Stack with LMCache KV Offloading

questions.question: How does the workload convert a prompt length into KV blocks?
options: It stores one block for every engine
questions.explanation: The local conversion is ceil((prompt_tokens + KV_BLOCK_TOKENS - 1) / KV_BLOCK_TOKENS), with 16 tokens per block.

questions.question: When does the LMCACHE branch use its shared cache?
options: Never; LMCACHE is a reporting label
Only after all four engines fail
questions.explanation: LMCACHE checks cached_local first; if false and cached_lmcache is true, it pays blocks × 3 ms and restores the prefix locally.

questions.question: Which per-block delay does CPU_OFFLOAD add in the model?
options: 3.0 ms per block with no scaling
questions.explanation: CPU_OFFLOAD adds blocks * CPU_OFFLOAD_TIME_MS_PER_BLOCK * 0.1, using the declared 1.5 ms/block constant.

questions.question: What production problem is shared LMCache meant to address across four engines?
options: It increases decode rate by changing output_tokens
It removes all HBM capacity limits
questions.explanation: The shared_cache set is cluster-wide; another engine can recover a repeated prefix even when cached_local is false.

questions.question: What happens when a request's prefix is already cached on its selected engine?
options: It moves the prefix to the shared cache and counts a miss
It rejects the request because HBM is full
questions.explanation: The local-cache fast path sets prefill_ms=0 and increments re_prefills_avoided.

questions.question: Why can NATIVE_ONLY still redo prefill on another engine?
options: It uses a global cache with a one-block TTL
It changes prefix_id on every request
questions.explanation: NATIVE_ONLY can skip work only when cached_local is true; a prefix evicted locally on the newly selected engine is re-prefilled because no shared cache is consulted.
